subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a full temp artifact registry and janitor classification model, or only core runtime-critical temp-path guardrails plus a minimal provenance seam for plugins?
rationale: The request crosses runtime safety, agent harness APIs, cleanup authority, SQLite state policy, and plugin/ClawHub ownership, and current repository policy does not make that boundary automatic.

options.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
options.body: Implement durable runtime checks and a narrow SQLite-backed provenance API, then leave workflow-specific artifact classification to plugins or ClawHub unless the seam proves insufficient.

options.title: Full core temp registry
options.body: Make OpenClaw core own artifact classes, provenance storage, durable promotion, and cleanup/janitor semantics for OpenClaw-created temp files.

options.title: Only concrete temp-path bugs
options.body: Decline the broad model and handle future temp-backed runtime or data-loss reports as narrower doctor/runtime fixes.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus SQLite seam
recommendation.body: Implement durable runtime checks and a narrow SQLite-backed provenance API, then leave workflow-specific artifact classification to plugins or ClawHub unless the seam proves insufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already made the closest ClawHub/core scope decision and has the strongest sampled history across the affected product and runtime boundaries.
